about: The priest asks God to look favorably upon the offering and accept it, as He accepted the gifts of the just Abel, the sacrifice of Abraham, and what Melchisedech offered to Him. Genesis calls Melchisedech a priest of God most high, and it is the Canon that calls him a high priest.

s01.narrative: The priest spreads his hands and goes on.

s02.translation: Deign to look upon them with a gracious and serene countenance and to regard them as accepted, as You deigned to accept the gifts of Your righteous servant Abel and the sacrifice of our Patriarch Abraham:

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s03.translation: and what Your high priest Melchisedech offered to You: a holy sacrifice, a spotless Victim.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

w016.explanation: With “dignátus” it forms the single predicate “Thou hast vouchsafed”.

w020.note: “Iusti” can be linked to the name Abel, “righteous Abel,” or to “púeri,” “Your righteous servant.” Both readings refer to the same person, and the adjective’s form does not determine the attachment.

w031.explanation: In Genesis 14:18 Melchisedech is called “sacérdos Dei altíssimi” — “priest of God most high”.

w034.explanation: Genesis 14:18 presents Melchisedech as priest of God most high, who brought out bread and wine.
